subject.title: fix(clawhub): SSRF-guard untrusted skill archive download URLs

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally fail closed for a self-hosted registry that returns an off-origin archive URL reachable only on private infrastructure?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent, but this is a deliberate compatibility and operator-policy choice: accepting those URLs would retain an SSRF-capable trust boundary, while rejecting them can require self-hosted deployments to change their archive topology.

options.title: Adopt origin as the trust boundary
options.body: Merge the fail-closed policy: same-origin registry archives may use the authenticated path, while every off-origin archive must pass the shared SSRF guard.

options.title: Support private artifact topology explicitly
options.body: Pause this PR and define a narrowly authenticated, documented self-hosted archive contract before allowing an off-origin private host.

recommendation.title: Adopt origin as the trust boundary
recommendation.body: Merge the fail-closed policy: same-origin registry archives may use the authenticated path, while every off-origin archive must pass the shared SSRF guard.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a core security and compatibility policy decision rather than a mechanical repair choice.
